# Code Interpreter

# Websearch

Websearch is the capability to **browse the web in search of information**, this tool does not only fix the limitations of models of not being up to date due to their training data, but also allows them to actually retrieve recent information or access specific websites.

A handy tool for any agent that needs to be up to date with the world.

<Image
  url={['/img/websearch_connector.png', '/img/websearch_connector_dark.png']}
  alt="websearch_graph"
  width="400px"
  centered
/>

Our built-in [tool](/studio/agents/agent-tools#built-in-tools) for websearch allows any of our models to access the web at any point to search websites and sources for relevant information to answer the given query.

There are two versions:
- `web_search`: A simple web search tool that enables access to a search engine.
- `web_search_premium`: A more complex web search tool that enables access to both a search engine and to news articles via integrated news provider verification.

:::warning
`web_search` and `web_search_premium` work with the [Conversations API](/studio/connectors/conversations) (`/v1/conversations`) and the Agents API. They aren't **supported** in the Chat Completions API (`/v1/chat/completions`) because Chat Completions responses don't include the search result references that these tools return.
:::

<SectionTab as="h1" sectionId="domain-filtering">Domain filtering</SectionTab>

An Organization admin can restrict which websites `web_search` returns, using an allowlist or a blocklist. Filtering is applied to the search results before your agent sees them, including when `web_search` runs inside `web_search_premium`.

Filtered results are removed silently. They are not returned, not cited, and not visible to the model, and the response carries no indication that anything was removed. If every result is dropped, the search returns nothing at all. This is most likely when your Organization uses an allowlist.

The same lists cover `open_url`: a request for a blocked domain is refused with `451 Unavailable For Legal Reasons` instead of being fetched.

To configure the lists, or to check whether your Organization has any, see [Web search domain filtering](/admin/identity-access/web-search-domain-filtering).

Another tool that uses references is the Document Library tool. For details, see the [Libraries guide](/studio/search/libraries#connecting-libraries-to-agents).
For more on citations, see the [citations guide](/studio/conversations/citations).

# Libraries

Libraries are persistent knowledge bases that you can fill with documents and connect to your agents for built-in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Upload PDFs, papers, or any document, and your agents can search through them on demand.

This page covers how to create Libraries, upload documents, index web pages, check processing status, and control access.

:::tip
You can also use Libraries created in Vibe: the Library ID is visible in the URL (`https://chat.mistral.ai/libraries/<library_id>`). To let an agent access a Vibe Library, you need to be an Org admin and share it with the Organization. The reverse also works: create a Library via the API and share it with your team in Vibe.
:::

<SectionTab as="h1" sectionId="adding-web-pages">Indexing a website</SectionTab>

You can create a Library directly from a website using the focused web crawler. The crawler fetches text content from the seed URL and follows child links up to a configurable depth.

:::note
From Mistral Studio, document processing is billed on a pay-as-you-go basis, the same as when you use the Mistral API.
:::

To index a website from [Studio](https://console.mistral.ai/libraries):

1. Click **Index a website**.
2. Enter a **Library Name** and the **Website URL** to crawl.
3. Optionally click **Advanced Settings** to configure the crawl.
4. Click **Start Indexing**.

The crawler extracts text content only. Images and charts are not indexed. To include visual content, download the page and upload it as a file instead.

<SectionTab as="h2" variant="secondary" sectionId="advanced-indexing-settings">Advanced indexing settings</SectionTab>

| Setting | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Maximum Pages** | Maximum number of pages to crawl from the seed URL. Range: 1-10000. |
| **Maximum Depth** | How many link hops from the seed URL to follow. Range: 1–10. Default: 10. |
| **URL filter rules** | Include or exclude rules that control which URLs are crawled. |
| **Refresh Schedule** | Automatic re-indexing frequency: None, Hourly, Daily, Weekly, or Monthly. |
| **Browser-based fetching** | Use a headless browser to render JavaScript-heavy pages before extracting content. Disabled by default. |

<SectionTab as="h1" sectionId="controlling-access">Controlling access</SectionTab>

You can manage who has access to each Library. Access control uses these parameters:

- `org_id` — your organization ID.
- `level` — the access level: `"Viewer"` or `"Editor"`.
- `share_with_uuid` — the ID of the entity you're sharing with (find these in your console and platform settings).
- `share_with_type` — the entity type: `"User"`, `"Workspace"`, or `"Org"`.

A few rules:
- You must be the Library owner to share it.
- An owner can't delete their own access.
- You must be the Library owner to delete someone else's access.
- Viewers can't edit Libraries. Editors can.

<SectionTab as="h2" variant="secondary" sectionId="understanding-the-response">Understanding the response</SectionTab>

The response contains two types of entries:

- **`tool.execution`** — the Document Library tool ran a search. Includes `name`, timestamps (`created_at`, `completed_at`), and a unique `id`.

- **`message.output`** — the agent's answer, grounded in the documents it found. The `content` field is a list of chunks that can be `text` (the actual response) or `tool_reference` (citations pointing back to source documents). Citations are useful for verifiable, traceable outputs.

The `usage` object shows token counts, including `connector_tokens` consumed by the Library search.

:::tip
The [web search](/studio/agents/agent-tools/websearch) tool also uses references. For more on citations, see the [citations guide](/studio/conversations/citations).
:::
